messages.content: Who are the famous dancers of the 19th Century?

function.name: get_museum_artists
function.description: Retrieves a list of all artists whose works are present in a museum during a particular period. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

period.description: The time period for which to retrieve the artists, e.g., 19th Century.

message.content:
**Famous Dancers of the 19th Century**

| Name | Nationality | Notable Contributions / Roles |
|------|-------------|--------------------------------|
| **Marie Taglioni** (1804–1884) | Swedish-Italian | Pioneered the “en pointe” technique; star of *La Sylphide* (1832). |
| **Fanny Elssler** (1810–1871) | Austrian | Renowned for her virtuosity and dramatic flair; performed across Europe and the U.S. |
| **Carlotta Grisi** (1819–1893) | Italian | Star of *Giselle* (1841) and *La Sylphide*; known for lyrical style. |
| **Enrico Cecchetti** (1850–1928) | Italian | Developed the Cecchetti method, a foundational ballet training system. |
| **Marius Petipa** (1818–1910) | Russian | Chief choreographer of the Imperial Ballet; created classics like *Swan Lake* and *The Nutcracker*. |
| **Jean Coralli** (1797–1865) | French | Co‑choreographer of *Giselle*; influential in Parisian ballet. |
| **Martha Graham** (1894–1991) | American | Though her career peaked in the 20th century, she was born in the 19th century and later revolutionized modern dance. |
| **Anna Pavlova** (1881–1931) | Russian | Though active mainly in the early 20th century, she was born in the 19th century and became one of the most celebrated ballerinas. |
| **John L. T. (John L. T.)** | American | A prominent figure in early American dance, especially in the minstrel and vaudeville circuits. |
| **George Balanchine** (1904–1983) | Russian-American | Born in the 20th century but his early training began in the late 19th‑early 20th century; later became a key figure in ballet. |

> **Note:** While some of the names above were born in the 19th century, their most influential work often extended into the early 20th century. The 19th century was a formative period for ballet, with many dancers laying the groundwork for modern techniques and repertoires.
